tldr: Google DeepMind released a substantial human-guided, machine-checked Signal verification study, while fresh agent-infrastructure, security-fingerprinting, research-review and small-model-learning preprints propose new techniques.

Reports on semiconductor bottlenecks, deep-sea robot trials, UK surveillance funding and French chatbot-regulation proposals broaden the picture; author results, company claims and advisory recommendations remain explicitly qualified.
Four source reports date to November 10 and five to November 9; catalog proposals (three tools, three concepts) remain deferred until canonical review.

news.title: DeepMind releases AlphaProof Code proofs for Signal's core cryptography
news.summary: Google DeepMind presented AlphaProof Code, a human-guided multi-agent framework using Lean-checked proof artifacts to connect defined cryptographic guarantees with compiled AArch64 libsignal code, covering PQXDH and Triple Ratchet properties.
news.why_it_matters: A notable demonstration of scaling verification beyond abstract protocol design into executable code.
news.caveat: It does not certify the entire Signal app or unspecified properties. The proofs depend on trusted human-approved specifications, model assumptions and the Lean kernel.

news.title: Evolving Infra proposes workload-adaptive prefill, decode and KV-cache management
news.summary: A November 9 preprint introduces dynamic prefill/decode GPU role switching and context-aware cache retention for agent workloads. Authors report up to 4.1x lower mean latency and 14x lower P95 time-to-first-token than their selected NVIDIA Dynamo setups.
news.why_it_matters: Long-running agent tasks often reuse prefixes after subagent work or pauses that recency-only cache eviction cannot anticipate.
news.caveat: These are unreplicated preprint maxima on selected workloads with up to 256 GB300 GPUs; a downloadable release was not verified.

news.title: Shibboleth research fingerprints attacking agent models and harnesses
news.summary: Researchers describe honeypot services that elicit characteristic language, command timeouts and tool-call behavior from an autonomous attacker. In controlled experiments they report 90% top-1 model classification across 15 candidates and 92% harness identification across four harnesses.
news.why_it_matters: Defenders may infer which tools or models drive an attack without direct access to the attacker's prompts or agent logs.
news.caveat: Controlled testing is not evidence of a real incident or universal attribution; the linked code repository was empty when checked.

news.title: PARIS research proposes a human-gated agent workflow for systematic reviews
news.summary: The PARIS preprint describes specialized review agents coordinated through persisted artifacts, three human checkpoints and a pre-synthesis corpus-quality measure. Two case studies reveal both useful workflows and retrieval/count-tracking failures.
news.why_it_matters: Auditable study selection and human oversight matter more than presenting an AI-generated research summary as a completed systematic review.
news.caveat: Unreviewed preprint: only eight of 27 PRISMA items fully supported, manuscripts judged internally, and the referenced public repository returned 404.

news.title: SCALE tests small-model-first learning from selectively triggered LLM reflection
news.summary: A November 9 preprint proposes a small model for routine agent decisions, using larger-model reflection on failures to create reusable conceptual knowledge and archive old experiences.
news.why_it_matters: Selectively internalizing experience could reduce recurring large-model calls in long-running agents.
news.caveat: Author-controlled experiments only; model generalization, deployed resource costs and independent reproducibility remain unverified.

news.title: Chipmakers say AI investment is squeezing mature automotive chip supply
news.summary: Reuters reports remarks by Nexperia and STMicroelectronics executives at Munich's Electronica conference about capacity shifting toward AI data centers and robotics, constraining automotive and industrial semiconductors.
news.why_it_matters: AI compute expansion affects manufacturing capacity outside the accelerator market.
news.caveat: These are named executives' observations, not a global quantitative inventory audit; remarks span November 9–10.

news.title: Impossible Metals reports trial of autonomous deep-sea mineral retrieval
news.summary: Reuters reports the company's claim that its autonomous robotic collector retrieved about 450 grams of nodules at over 4,000 meters depth during a September 2026 Pacific test.
news.why_it_matters: An early example of AI-guided autonomy in a challenging underwater environment, with significant environmental oversight issues.
news.caveat: Company-reported controlled test; claims of reduced environmental harm are not independently verified, and commercial operations require approval.

news.title: UK announces £90 million for AI-enabled undersea surveillance
news.summary: Reuters reports a British plan for AI, drones and sensors to monitor threats to North Atlantic undersea infrastructure.
news.why_it_matters: Autonomous detection and sensor fusion are being pursued for security of critical infrastructure.
news.caveat: Funding announcement only; not evidence of completed fielding or measured effectiveness.

news.title: French AI council urges stronger protections for chatbot users
news.summary: Le Monde reports CIANum's November 10 advisory recommendations for stronger protections for minors, transparency about commercial influence and user profiling, and pre-market vulnerability assessments.
news.why_it_matters: Policy debate is moving toward how personalized conversational assistants affect users, not just training-data or model-level controls.
news.caveat: Advisory proposals are not law; original council report was not accessed independently.
